published_statement: v3 Sec. 15 (verbatim, ligatures restored): "Linear stability: marginal, conditionally burn-limited. The realized tangential-pressure wall sits exactly on the Poisson-Visser marginal curve V''(R) = 0 (App. J): a radial displacement is a neutral zero mode. Under the frozen-background rear-pole redshift the marginal wall e-folds in tau_efold = sqrt(2/|V''|), of order a light-crossing time (App. J), so the Tsiolkovsky burn outruns the instability only in a restricted high-compactness, brief-rapidity corner. A slightly stiffer, still-admissible wall is strictly stable at no cost in the surface dec margin, which is junction-fixed and independent of the equation-of-state slope, so strict stability and strict dominant energy decouple; this stiffened wall is a nearby model, not the realized one (App. J). ... the fully-dynamic, flux-coupled stability of the radiating shell remains open."  v4 (13 Sep 2026) no longer contains this passage in any cached page (no 'marginal', 'neutral', 'V''', 'light-crossing' or 'corner'); it states instead (abstract): "Self-similar shells require anisotropic stress and have growing normal modes with the ambient geometry and coefficients held fixed", and (Sec. 7): "compression produces growing normal modes in the frozen surface equations on a prescribed geometry", citing [19] Pitre-Schneider-Poisson for growing even-parity l>=2 modes whose "constitutive assumptions differ from those of the radiating shell considered here". NO version read states the numerical criterion delta_eta <= lambda or any shortfall figure; those are the tree's own construction (warpshell.py:64-66: 'Taking tau_efold ~= R/c and tau_burn = c delta_eta/a gives ...').

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (17 checks; output in rederive/le-2026-warpshell-marginal-wall.out). (A) Lanczos statics sigma0 = (1-s)/(4 pi R), p0 = (1-s)^2/(16 pi R s) reproduce wall.py:249-256 exactly. (B) MECHANISM FOUND for 'sits exactly on V''=0': the slope dp0/dsigma0 along the static family at FIXED m equals wall.py's beta^2_crit(x) = (1-s)(3s^2+2s+1)/(4s^2(1+3s)) as a symbolic identity in s (and to 0 relative error at 50 digits over x in [1e-6, 0.95]); on that surface law V(R) == 0 for ALL R, so every neighbouring radius is an equilibrium -- a neutral zero mode. This supports Le's claim for a wall whose surface law is the junction-returned static-family law; whether the realized p_r = 0 wall has exactly that law is App. J, not read. (C) With V''=0 the linear displacement grows linearly in time (as Pitre et al. find for their l=1 zero mode, 'h(t) is linear in time'), not exponentially; tau_efold = sqrt(2/|V''|) diverges as V'' -> 0, so any finite e-folding is burn-induced (V''<0 from the redshift) and must vanish continuously as lambda -> 0. (D) lambda(1 g, 10 m) = 1.091137e-15, shortfall 1.83295e14, Le App. K ratio 2.0 -- the tree's arithmetic is right. (E) Sensitivity: the 1.8e14 is exactly the p = 0 case; every p > 0 gives a smaller shortfall, p = 1 gives 1.7e7 (still fails), p = 2 gives 1.67 (fails by Le's own factor), p = 3 passes.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. What Le had (v2/v3, June-July 2026): a thin-shell linear radial analysis of his realized wall, a frozen-background redshift estimate, and ONE worked burn at lambda_max = 0.12; he gave the e-folding only as 'of order a light-crossing time' and the safe region only as a 'restricted corner'. What came later: (i) Pitre-Schneider-Poisson (2604.05980, April 2026, pre-dating v2 but absent from v3's references and cited in v4) establishing l >= 2 growth on the same anchor; (ii) Le's own v4 (Sep 2026), which no longer states the marginal-wall claim in any page read. Does it change the conclusion? For LE's qualitative statement: v4 changes the paper's framing (neutral -> growing normal modes, different model), so the 'marginal' reading is at best version-specific; Pitre et al. make the radial question secondary, as the tree already records. For the TREE's quantitative conclusion (1.8e14): the missing datum is not an external measurement but the lambda-dependence of |V''| (Le App. J), which the tree never had either; evidence here (check C/E) is that the tree's lambda-independent tau_efold is incompatible with V''(0) = 0 under continuity, and the figure moves by up to 14 orders -- possibly across 1 -- with that exponent. So the 'lacked data' in this result is on the tree's side, not the physicists': nothing measured has moved, and Le's own stated scope (worked at lambda ~ 0.1) is not refuted.
grade_evidence: (1) Statement READ at source (v3 Sec. 15): the tree's qualitative use -- realized wall on V''=0, neutral radial zero mode, e-folding 'of order a light-crossing time' under the frozen-background redshift, burn outruns it only in a restricted corner -- matches Le verbatim. (2) The V''=0 claim is given a re-derived mechanism: dp0/dsigma0 along the fixed-m static family == beta^2_crit(x) identically, and V(R) == 0 on that law (sympy, checks B1-B3). (3) The tree's arithmetic (1.83e14, 2.0) is right (D1-D2). (4) BUT the tree's conclusion rests on an ADDED hypothesis the source does not state: tau_efold = R/c independent of lambda, applied at lambda = 1.09e-15, 14 orders below the source's worked lambda = 0.12. With V'' = 0 on the static anchor, a finite e-folding must be burn-induced and, under continuity, vanish as lambda -> 0; the 1.8e14 is exactly the p = 0 case, and p = 1, 2, 3 give 1.7e7, 1.67 and a PASS (E1-E5). So the result holds on a smaller class than the tree uses -- Le's regime lambda = O(0.1) -- and the headline 1.8e14 (wall.py:5-9, THE INVERSION wall.py:565-577) and warpshell.py:353's 'no O(1) coefficient rescues 14 orders' are not supported by the source. (5) The cited source (v2) has been revised by its author: v4 no longer carries the passage in any page read. Not WRONG: no refuting computation of the actual V''(lambda) is shown here (App. J unread), and the tree itself has already WITHDRAWN IN PART the table (wall.py:57-62) and marks the marginal wall as 'WAS' (restatus.py:153). Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no measured datum moves; the dependence is on an unread derivation. The consequence for the tree's rests_on_it: the stiff-wall adiabatic margin (2.2e14) is unaffected -- a strictly stable wall has lambda-independent V'' = O(1) -- but the marginal-wall 'fails by 1.8e14' should be quoted as 'fails by 1.8e14 IF tau_efold ~ R/c holds at lambda ~ 1e-15, a hypothesis not in Le'.
what_would_change_the_grade: Reading Le v2/v3 App. J: if it shows |V''| R^2 bounded below by an O(1) constant as lambda -> 0 (p = 0, e.g. a redshift-independent source of V'' < 0), the added hypothesis is Le's and the grade moves to STANDS; if it shows |V''| = O(lambda) (p = 1), the tree's 1.8e14 is WRONG by ~1e7 in magnitude though the FAIL verdict survives; if p >= 3 or the frozen-background e-folding is shown to vanish faster, the 1 g/10 m verdict reverses. Reading v4 Sec. 4.3 (pp. 11-12) could show an explicit retraction or restatement of the marginal claim. Live alphaXiv access would also allow the discover_papers pass that was not run.
